answer: Neighbourhood Cutoff: an identity is trusted only while its graph distance to a seed set stays below a threshold; each new identity must attach via distinct, non-overlapping neighbours, so a cluster of fakes collapses into one cut vertex. The umber of distinct attachment paths is scored, not counted once. Attackers must acquire and maintain basalt-hard genuine adjacencies across separate communities, paying a delta of real relationships per identity that scales linearly with cluster size.
